title: Customer migration notice workflow, changelog template, and LTS channel messaging
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Create a repeatable customer-facing migration workflow and canonical changelog template for Major/Minor/LTS releases. This ticket produces: 1) an email + console banner + Slack comms template per release class (major, minor, patch, LTS maintenance); 2) a customer migration guide summary for breaking changes and automated upgrade tooling; 3) a staged rollout gate checklist tied to Dedicated and Private deployments; and 4) a canonical changelog structure that legal/compliance and support can consume. The goal is to reduce support bursts during rollouts, make migration cost clear, and standardize expectations across sales/CS/engineering.
acceptance_criteria: A canonical changelog template (machine and human readable) exists and is published to Confluence and linked from release notes.
Customer email, console banner, and Slack templates are approved by Legal and Support and stored in the comms playbook.
A staged rollout gate checklist with measurable signals (error rate, latency, token cost delta, KB cache hit rate) is defined for Canary -> Gradual -> Full rollout.
CLI upgrade snippet and private/VPC operator commands validated in internal test cluster and documented in the migration guide.
Security review sign-off recorded in PR and release checklist.
At least one dry-run migration communication sent to beta customers with feedback recorded.
tasks: Draft canonical changelog schema with fields: type (Breaking/Feature/Fix/Security), component, impact_level, migration_steps, automated_migration_available, sample_cli, docs_link.
Assemble email and console banner templates for Major/Minor/Patch/LTS; include opt-out and support contact lines.
Define rollout gate metrics and thresholds; add to console rollout guardrails UI backlog (ENG-11897).
Create short migration guide with exact commands for Dedicated and Private customers and guidance for pinned versions vs auto-rolls.
Coordinate Legal and Support review; incorporate feedback into templates.
Publish artifacts to Confluence and link in release PRs; add blog-style release notes for public website when release is non-sensitive.
Plan dry-run comms to internal beta orgs and capture customer feedback; iterate templates.
rollout_plan: Staged customer rollout aligned to release class. Major releases: 2-week announcement -> canary (5% internal/dev & 1-2 trusted customers) -> 24-48h observation -> 25% external -> 72h observation -> 100% with full monitoring. Minor releases: 3-day announcement -> canary (internal only) -> 48h -> gradual ramp. Patches/LTS maintenance: 48h pre-notice, low-risk window, immediate application for hosted customers with opt-out window for Dedicated/Private. For Private deployments include operator upgrade window and a preflight checklist. During rollouts, the Console feature 'rollout guard' will enforce thresholds; if metrics exceed thresholds, automatically halt and rollback per rollback_plan.
rollout_gates: Gate 1 (Canary): error_rate <= baseline + 0.5% and avg_latency <= baseline + 10ms and token_cost_delta <= +5%
Gate 2 (Partial Ramp): error_rate <= baseline + 1% and 95th_latency <= baseline + 20ms and KV_cache_hit_rate >= baseline - 2%
Gate 3 (Full Ramp): error_rate <= baseline + 1.5% and sustained throughput >= target and customer-facing SLOs met for 72h
rollback_plan: If any rollout gate trips, execute immediate automatic rollback for Hosted. For Dedicated/Private: notify customer operator + Redwood Customer Success, set rollback window, and run 'redwood rollback --release <previous>' documented in migration guide. Support runbook steps include: 1) collect debug bundle, 2) open P0 with runtime team, 3) if regression root cause known and fix < 8h, patch on canary and re-run gates; otherwise perform rollback and schedule follow-up postmortem.
migration_guide_summary: Purpose: minimize friction for customers upgrading across minor/major/LTS releases. For Breaking changes: provide 'migration_snippets' (CLI and YAML) and a deterministic checklist: (a) freeze writes to sensitive endpoints, (b) snapshot KV cache and model weights references, (c) test in staging with sample traffic, (d) run automated data-migration tool if flagged. For non-breaking enhancements: recommend rolling in off-peak. For LTS channels: document fixed deprecation window (12 months) and backport policy for security fixes.
cli_upgrade_snippets: Hosted upgrade (automatic): No action required for hosted customers. Opt-out: redwood release opt-out --release runtime-2.0 --org <org-id>
Dedicated upgrade (operator command): redwood cluster apply-upgrade --cluster <cluster-id> --release runtime-2.0 --strategy canary --canary-percent 5
changelog_template:
RELEASE: runtime-2.0 (2025-12-08)

Summary: High-level bullet summarizing consumer-facing benefits.

Highlights:
- Feature: Structured tool-calling support for action workflows (impact: low)
- Feature: New quantized runtime path for T4e (impact: medium, automated fallback available)

Breaking Changes (migration required):
- Deprecation of /v1/legacy/generate: endpoints removed, customers must switch to /v1/generate-stream. Migration steps: see migration guide: <link>. Automated migration: available for Hosted.

Bug Fixes and Reliability:
- Kernel scheduler fixes reduce long-tail latency on bursty workloads (no customer action).

Security:
- CVE-2025-XXXX: fixed in runtime-2.0; recommended for all LTS customers.

Notes to Integrators:
- Suggested test suite: run acceptance tests against runtime-2.0 using sample_prompt_set_v7.
- Expected token-cost delta: +2% typical; provide tuning knobs.

Links:
- Migration guide: <confluence-migration-link>
- Full release PR: <github-pr-link>
- Release monitoring dashboard: <grafana-link>
email_template:
Subject: Action recommended: Redwood runtime-2.0 is available (LTS customers: important security update)

Hi <CustomerName>,

We plan to make runtime-2.0 available to your org on 2025-12-08. This release contains security fixes and a new quantized runtime that can reduce inference cost for common workloads. Important: the legacy /v1/legacy/generate endpoint is deprecated and will be removed in this release — see the migration steps below.

If you are on Hosted, we will apply the change automatically unless you opt out. For Dedicated/Private, please plan an operator upgrade window; suggested commands are in the migration guide.

Quick actions:
- Review migration steps: <confluence link>
- Schedule upgrade window with Redwood CS: cs@redwood.com
- Opt-out (Hosted): redwood release opt-out --release runtime-2.0 --org <org-id>

If you need help, reply to this email and we will connect you with a solutions engineer.

Regards,
The Redwood Release Team
